# Hippius

> Hippius is a distributed cloud: encrypted file storage (Drive), S3-compatible object storage, a registry for AI models and containers (Hub), a CDN, and confidential compute (VMs, managed PostgreSQL, managed Kubernetes, GitHub Actions runners). One account pays for all of them. From a terminal, `hipc` is the one command for the whole account. This file says how an agent works with Hippius, what each product is, and which file to open next.

Open only the file for the product you need. The long reference for the whole product, including the Object Storage manual, is [llms-full.txt](https://docs.hippius.com/llms-full.txt)

## Instructions for agents

- If you can run commands, install `hipc` and use it instead of calling https://api.hippius.com directly.
- The user runs `hipc auth login` in their own terminal. Never ask for the API token, a 12-word key, or a password in the chat.
- Read https://docs.hippius.com/cli/agents once before the first command.
- Find a command with `hipc --help`, one level at a time, or `hipc schema <path>`, such as `hipc schema s3 buckets`; don't recall flags from memory or from a web page.
- Run every write with `--dry-run` first, and ask the user before adding `--yes`.

Install: `brew install thenervelab/tap/hipc`, or `curl -fsSL https://github.com/thenervelab/hippius-cli/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sh`, or `pip install hippius` (the PyPI package `hippius` installs the same `hipc` command).

- [hipc for agents](https://docs.hippius.com/cli/agents): the one page to read first; raw Markdown at https://raw.githubusercontent.com/thenervelab/hippius-cli/main/docs/agents.md
- [Accounts and projects](https://docs.hippius.com/cli/agents/accounts), [Secrets](https://docs.hippius.com/cli/agents/secrets), [Hub](https://docs.hippius.com/cli/agents/hub), [hipc api](https://docs.hippius.com/cli/agents/api): read one only when the task needs it
- [Finding a command](https://docs.hippius.com/cli/commands), [Examples](https://docs.hippius.com/cli/examples)

## Which file to open

| Want to | Open |
|---|---|
| Manage the account, projects, billing, plans, S3 buckets and keys, Hub, compute and App Engine apps, Kubernetes, databases, runners, CDN, the private network, or support from a terminal or an agent | [hipc](https://docs.hippius.com/cli), as above |
| Store or fetch files from code, rclone, or a backup tool | [hippius-s3 llms.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/thenervelab/hippius-s3/staging/llms.txt) |
| Store encrypted files in the browser (Drive) | [Drive guide](https://docs.hippius.com/use/drive) |
| Back up photos or a folder from a computer or phone | Drive with the [desktop app](https://docs.hippius.com/use/desktop/getting-started) or the iPhone or Android app; first steps under Account, sign-in, and paying, below |
| Publish or pull a model or a container image | [hippius-hub llms.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/thenervelab/hippius-hub/main/llms.txt); the namespace, plan, and CI keys are also `hipc hub` |
| Sync folders on a computer | [hippius-desktop llms.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/thenervelab/hippius-desktop/staging/llms.txt) |
| Work in a shared drive | A Drive someone else owns and invited you into. They pay for the storage. It shows in the console under Storage after the invite. |
| Give a coding agent shared memory | [hippius-mem llms.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/thenervelab/hippius-mem/main/llms.txt) |
| Script Drive with encryption on the client | [hippius-drive-sdk llms.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/thenervelab/hippius-drive-sdk/main/llms.txt) |
| Sign up, pay, get an API token, or manage Drive and S3 keys in the browser | [Console getting started](https://docs.hippius.com/use/console/getting-started) |
| Bridge Alpha on subnet 75 to hAlpha, then buy balance with it | [Fund with Alpha](https://docs.hippius.com/use/console/fund-with-alpha) |
| Understand paying with Bittensor subnet 75 gamma through the API (not live yet) | [Pay with Gamma](https://docs.hippius.com/use/pay-with-gamma) |
| Use Drive on an iPhone or Android phone | [Mobile getting started](https://docs.hippius.com/use/mobile/getting-started) |
| Run a VM, managed PostgreSQL, managed Kubernetes or GitHub Actions runners (Compute) | `hipc compute`, and the [Compute guide](https://docs.hippius.com/use/compute) |
| Serve an S3 bucket through the CDN (zones on <zone>.c.hipcdn.net or your own domain; FR $0.010/GB, AU $0.060/GB, $0.002 per 10,000 requests, $1/month per custom domain) | `hipc cdn`, and the [CDN guide](https://docs.hippius.com/use/cdn) |
| Filter requests to a CDN zone with a WAF: custom rules, rate limits, IP/ASN/country lists (every zone, Security tab; Standard $5, Advanced $20 per zone per month) | `hipc cdn waf`, and the [WAF guide](https://docs.hippius.com/use/cdn/firewall) |
| Read compute, CDN, Object Storage, Drive and Hub prices without an account (GET https://api.hippius.com/api/compute/public-prices/, no auth; `hipc` reads the plan lists with no token), or sign users in with their 12-word access key from your own app | [Management API](https://docs.hippius.com/use/api), which links the Public Price API and Access Key Sign-In API pages |
| Let team members use your compute, Object Storage and CDN, or work in an account you were invited to (shared accounts) | `hipc account`, [Accounts and projects](https://docs.hippius.com/cli/agents/accounts), and the [Shared accounts guide](https://docs.hippius.com/use/console/team) |
| Run a storage miner | [Miner guide](https://docs.hippius.com/earn/arion/running-miner) and [arion llms.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/thenervelab/arion/main/llms.txt) |
| Run a validator | [Validator guide](https://docs.hippius.com/earn/installing-validator) |

## Account, sign-in, and paying

Full console guide: [Console getting started](https://docs.hippius.com/use/console/getting-started)
Billing: [Billing guide](https://docs.hippius.com/use/console/billing)

- One account covers the console, the desktop app, the mobile app, and `hipc`. Sign-in is Google, GitHub, Apple, or an existing 12-word access key. There is no email and password sign-in.
- The API token, for Hub, the account API and `hipc`, depends on how the user signs in:
  - Google, GitHub or Apple: the user copies it from console Settings, https://console.hippius.com/dashboard/settings, and stores it with `hipc auth login` in their own terminal. An agent cannot do this sign-in for them.
  - A 12-word access key: Settings does not show a token for this sign-in. The access-key sign-in (POST /api/auth/mnemonic/, then POST /api/auth/verify/ on api.hippius.com; steps: https://docs.hippius.com/use/wallet-login) signs a challenge with the key and returns a token; an agent that holds its own key does this sign-in itself, and its first verify creates the account, so one mistyped word opens a new, empty account. `hipc` never takes the 12 words: the token that sign-in returns goes to `hipc auth login`. Never ask for the 12 words in chat.
  - For CI or a server, sign in once on a machine you trust and store only the token (as the secret `HIPPIUS_TOKEN`). Never put the 12 words on a runner: they control the whole account and its funds.
- A 12-word access key creates a wallet-only account. It has no real email address, so it gets no lifecycle mail. Drive has no free plan: subscribe before the first upload. Object Storage and Hub work the same as on any other account.
- S3 endpoint is https://s3.hippius.com only. Keys (the access key id starts with `hip_`) are created with `hipc s3 tokens`, or on the console Object Storage page: https://docs.hippius.com/use/console/s3. For an app, prefer a sub token scoped to its bucket; a master token reaches every bucket and bypasses bucket ACLs. The secret is shown once: write it to a private file rather than to stdout, and `hipc s3 configure` turns the token into an AWS CLI profile. https://docs.hippius.com/cli/agents/secrets
- Hub has a second credential, the registry robot login, created when the namespace is provisioned (`hipc hub namespace create`, or `hippius-hub`). For CI, create a scoped key with `hipc hub keys` instead of sharing that login, and log in with `docker login registry.hippius.com -u '<login>' --password-stdin`. Single-quote the login: it contains a `$`. https://docs.hippius.com/cli/agents/hub, GitHub Actions: https://docs.hippius.com/registry/ci
- Drive encryption uses an unlock password and a 12-word recovery seed. Never ask the user to paste either into chat.
- 1 credit = $1: a price or cap given in credits, such as a CDN spend cap, is in dollars. 1 USDC adds one dollar to your balance. Topping up fills the balance. It does not add storage. Subscribe to a plan for that. https://docs.hippius.com/use/console/billing
- Top up on Billing in one of five ways. Card, through Stripe, from $10 to $10,000, or a monthly auto reload (`hipc billing top-up` with a card prints the checkout URL). Bitcoin, on-chain or Lightning, from $20 to $100,000. Lightning lands in seconds; on-chain after one confirmation. USDC on Base from a browser wallet, from $5 to $10,000; 1 USDC adds one dollar to your balance. TAO, from a connected wallet or by sending to the TAO deposit address (Manually tab), at least $20 per transfer; never send TAO to the Hippius account address, which is not credited. A transfer cannot be reversed. hAlpha (Hippius native token), on the Hippius tab: credits = hAlpha × the on-chain hAlpha price, 1% slippage protection by default, final on chain with no refund. `hipc billing top-up` takes card, Bitcoin, or hAlpha. When the account is custodial (the API signs its buys; `hipc billing native-quote` says so), `hipc billing top-up` converts hAlpha into credits on chain: at least 0.01 hAlpha, and it cannot be undone. An account that signs its own buys (`custodial` false, such as an access-key account) buys in the console, or an agent that holds its key signs Marketplace.buy_credits itself and bridges Alpha on subnet 75 by signing the steps (no bridge CLI): https://docs.hippius.com/use/console/fund-with-alpha. USDC and TAO stay in the console. Those are browser wallet steps a person approves, so an agent cannot fund the balance with them on its own. https://docs.hippius.com/use/console/billing
- An agent with enough balance subscribes without a browser, with `hipc drive subscription`, `hipc s3 subscription`, or `hipc hub subscription`: dry-run it, and ask the user before the `--yes`. Plan codes: Drive `solo` (Starter), `duo` (Plus), `max`, `scale`; S3 `pro`, `business`, `enterprise`; Hub Free, Builder, Pro, Team (paid from the balance only). Moving from one paid plan to another is a change, not a second subscribe. The plan lists (`hipc drive plans`, `hipc s3 plans`, `hipc hub plans`) need no token. Card checkout is a browser; do not send a funded agent there.
- Google, GitHub, and Apple accounts include the Free Drive Plan (10 GB). Object Storage starts on pay as you go at $6 per TB per month, and a plan is optional.
- First steps for a new account that wants to back up photos or a folder: the Free plan's 10 GB is there at once (a 12-word access key account has none); for more, top up at least $10 on Billing, then subscribe to Drive Starter (`solo`, 500 GB, $4 a month); then install the desktop app (https://docs.hippius.com/use/desktop/getting-started) or the iPhone or Android app and sign in there. Drive uploads happen in those apps and need no API token; ask for a token only to read the plan or subscribe from `hipc`.
- Plan prices, monthly, from the balance (always current in the catalogs): Drive Free 10 GB $0, Starter 500 GB $4, Plus 2 TB $7, Max 10 TB $22, Scale 25 TB $50 (Max and Scale bill storage above the plan hourly, $2.20 and $2.00 per TB per month, up to a storage cap that defaults to twice the plan). Object Storage Pro 10 TB $53, Business 50 TB $245, Enterprise 100 TB $465 (pay as you go otherwise: $6 per TB per month). Hub Free $0, Builder $5, Pro $19, Team $99.
- Shared accounts: an owner invites members by email, with Viewer, Operator or Admin access per product (VMs, databases, Kubernetes, runners, Object Storage, CDN). The owner pays and the owner's quotas apply. Drive is not included. `hipc account list` shows the accounts a token can act in: https://docs.hippius.com/cli/agents/accounts https://docs.hippius.com/use/console/team
- Open a support ticket: `hipc support tickets`, or the console.

Hub Free plan: creating a namespace requires a balance of at least $10, a spam check. A zero balance is refused. The plan price stays zero. Top up, then provision. https://docs.hippius.com/use/console/hub

## Without hipc: the raw API

The OpenAPI spec is https://api.hippius.com/swagger.json. Header `Authorization: Token YOUR_TOKEN`, plus `X-Hippius-Account: acct_...` for a shared account (ids from GET https://api.hippius.com/api/accounts/). Subscribe routes: POST https://api.hippius.com/api/drive/subscription/ with `{"plan":"solo","period":"monthly","payment":"credits"}`; POST https://api.hippius.com/api/s3/subscription/ with `{"plan":"pro","rail":"credits"}`; GET https://api.hippius.com/api/registry/plans/ then POST https://api.hippius.com/api/registry/subscribe/ with `{"plan_id": 2}` (the API requires `plan_id`, not a name; Builder is id 2). 201 if the balance covers the plan. Support: POST https://api.hippius.com/api/support/tickets/ with subject, priority, category, and description. Send your own User-Agent: some default ones (Python urllib) are blocked with 403 error 1010.

## Deprecated

The IPFS-era command line (its `hipc storage` commands; the name `hipc` now belongs to the new CLI above), `hippius-sdk`, `hippius-sdk-ts`, `hippius-sdk-rust`, `hippius-rust-sdk`, `hippius-sync-engine`, `hippius-storage-miner`, the storage commands of the Python package `hippius` up to 0.2.77, and anything else IPFS-related, are deprecated. Hippius switched from IPFS to Arion. https://docs.hippius.com/cli/usage

Chain registration still uses the Python package `hippius` pinned to `hippius==0.2.77`: https://docs.hippius.com/earn/register-in-blockchain

## Compute

Confidential VMs on AMD SEV-SNP, managed PostgreSQL, managed Kubernetes and GitHub Actions runners, open to every account. Metered per second (one-minute minimum per VM and public IPv4), charged hourly on the Hippius chain from the account balance. A VM is billed from its launch until it is deleted, running or stopped. A launch needs a balance covering 24 hours of the account's compute plus the launch (https://docs.hippius.com/use/compute/billing#the-24-hour-balance-requirement), and quotas apply: new accounts start on the Starter tier and move up automatically with their charged usage.

An hour the balance cannot pay is recorded as unpaid debt that the account owes, and VMs keep running: the balance is not a spending cap. To limit what a project spends in a month, set a budget. The Default project has no budget: create a project, launch in it, and give it a budget (`hipc account projects`), which mails at each alert share and can refuse new launches that add cost once the limit is reached. It does not stop what already runs, which keeps being billed. The compute charge cap is the most the chain charges the account per hour, a safety limit, not a monthly budget.

From a terminal, the VMs, their catalog, quota, firewall, public IPv4, and SSH keys, the databases, Kubernetes, and runners are all under `hipc compute`; walk `hipc compute --help`. A VM launched by hipc has no firewall rule, so nothing reaches its public IPv4 until a port is opened, at launch or with a firewall update. Deleting a VM releases its public IPv4; stored backups stay billed until they are removed.

Prices per 730-hour month, on the default NVMe OS disk: vCPU $18, memory $2.50/GB, disk $0.10/GB. Small (1 vCPU, 4 GB, 40 GB) is $32 a month ($0.0438/h), Medium $64, Large $128, X-Large $256, 2X-Large $512, 4X-Large $1024. The OS disk tier is chosen at launch and fixed: SSD (disk $0.06/GB, Small $27.60, Medium $55.20, Large $110.40) or HDD, slow shared storage for dev and test, not for production or databases, offered up to Large (disk $0.03/GB, Small $17.16, Medium $34.32, Large $68.64). Dedicated disks (whole physical disks for one VM, up to 8, at least 1,000 GiB each; the VM is then pinned: no backups, migration or failover): $2.50 HDD, $5 SSD, $8 NVMe per TiB-month. Public IPv4 $0.005/h (~$3.65/month). VM backups $6 per TB-month. Outbound bandwidth is metered per region and not charged today; inbound is free. Managed databases cost their VMs plus 25%; Kubernetes costs its VMs plus $15 per cluster per month. The live price list wins: https://console.hippius.com/dashboard/billing/compute#prices

- Overview (quotas, the 24-hour balance requirement, billing): https://docs.hippius.com/use/compute
- Create a VM and connect over SSH or from the browser: https://docs.hippius.com/use/virtual-machines
- Public IPv4, firewall rules and published ports: https://docs.hippius.com/use/compute/networking
- Resize a VM (vCPU and memory; the disk is kept): https://docs.hippius.com/use/compute/resize
- VM backups and restore: https://docs.hippius.com/use/compute/vm-backups
- Dedicated disks (whole physical HDD/SSD/NVMe disks, exact tier, pinned VM, own quota): https://docs.hippius.com/use/compute/dedicated-disks
- VM failover: if a VM's server dies, the VM restarts on another server in the same region from its latest backup, keeping its IP and NetBird address; data since that backup is lost. Automatic failover is opt-in per VM, at creation (switch under Automatic backups; API `"failover_mode": "auto"` with `backup_interval_s`) or later in the Backups panel. Offered in France only today. Active after the first full backup: https://docs.hippius.com/use/compute/vm-failover
- Placement groups: VMs of one account in the same group (`placement_group` at creation, 1 to 64 of a-z, 0-9, -) are never on the same server. A different server is not a different datacenter. Fixed at creation: https://docs.hippius.com/use/compute/vm-failover#placement-groups
- Compute API, only without hipc: base https://api.hippius.com/api, header `Authorization: Token YOUR_TOKEN` (plus `X-Hippius-Account: acct_...` for a shared account). Full OpenAPI spec: https://api.hippius.com/swagger.json. Create a VM with POST /api/compute/vms/ `{"name":"web-1","flavor":"small","region":"FR","ssh_key_ids":[123]}` (keys from GET /api/ssh-keys/), then poll GET /api/compute/vms/<vm_id>/ until `status` is `running` and, with a public IPv4, `network_ready` is `true`, then SSH to the public IP (or to `netbird_ip` over NetBird). `status` is the lifecycle (billed while `running`, stopped included), `power_state` is on/off. Send your own User-Agent: some default ones (Python urllib) are blocked with 403 error 1010: https://docs.hippius.com/use/api#compute-api
- Managed PostgreSQL 16/17/18 (one-time credentials, TLS, backups to your Object Storage, restore, HA failover): https://docs.hippius.com/use/compute/databases
- Managed Kubernetes clusters (cluster key, kubeconfig, API access): https://docs.hippius.com/use/compute/kubernetes
- Kubernetes worker pools and signed node operations: https://docs.hippius.com/use/compute/kubernetes-worker-pools
- Kubernetes backups (etcd snapshots, Velero, restore with rclone): https://docs.hippius.com/use/compute/kubernetes-backups
- GitHub Actions runners (`runs-on: hippius-small|medium|large`, `-ssd` for the cheaper SSD tier; spend per day, repository, size and workflow, compared with GitHub-hosted runners): https://docs.hippius.com/use/compute/runners
- Compute prices, management fees, quotas and unpaid balance: https://docs.hippius.com/use/compute/billing
- Refusals and troubleshooting: https://docs.hippius.com/use/compute/troubleshooting

The Kubernetes cluster key is generated in the user's browser, so creating a cluster stays in the console; hipc lists, reads and deletes clusters, scales node pools and writes kubeconfigs. Database credentials are returned once at creation, and the server keeps no copy: `hipc compute databases create` writes them to private files with `--credentials-dir` (https://docs.hippius.com/cli/agents/secrets). A deleted database cannot be restored: take a `pg_dump` first. Never ask the user to paste a database secret into chat.
